title: Measurement-induced enhancement of the $X$-parity lifetime in a Majorana tetron
authors: Katharina Laubscher, Jay D. Sau, Sankar Das Sarma
abstract: A recent experiment [arXiv:2507.08795] has reported measurements of the interwire $X$-parity lifetime in a Majorana tetron device via the quantum capacitance of an auxiliary readout dot. Motivated by these measurements, we theoretically study the interwire parity lifetime in a minimal model of the coupled dot-tetron system subject to electrostatic noise. We show that coupling to the measurement dot can itself strongly modify the parity dynamics by generating an energy splitting that shifts noise-induced transitions to finite frequency and thereby stabilizes the measured states against low-frequency fluctuations. For representative noise strengths motivated by disordered nanowire devices, we find $X$-parity switching lifetimes of order microseconds in the measurement configuration even when the corresponding bare-tetron coherence time is only tens of nanoseconds long. We analyze both the dispersive regime, where the dot can be integrated out and the dynamics reduces to an effective two-level system, and the near-resonant regime, where all four low-energy states participate. In the latter case, rapid transitions organize the spectrum into two long-lived manifolds that approximately correspond to sectors of the combined dot-tetron $X$-loop parity, yielding effective two-state switching despite the underlying multilevel structure. Our results show that measurement-induced stabilization can substantially enhance the observed $X$-parity switching lifetime, such that the lifetime measured under continuous readout can greatly exceed the intrinsic idle $T_2^*$ coherence time of the isolated Majorana tetron qubit.
summary: This theoretical study models a Majorana tetron qubit coupled to a measurement dot to understand its parity lifetime. The authors demonstrate that the measurement coupling generates an energy splitting that effectively shields the qubit from low-frequency noise. This measurement-induced stabilization can dramatically extend the observable coherence time beyond the intrinsic coherence limit of the isolated qubit.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates how coupling a Majorana tetron qubit to an auxiliary measurement dot modifies the intrinsic $X$-parity lifetime.
main_result: Measurement coupling can stabilize the $X$-parity state, leading to measured lifetimes that significantly exceed the bare coherence time, even in the presence of noise.
method: The study uses a minimal model Hamiltonian, analyzing the system dynamics in both the dispersive and near-resonant regimes.
model_or_system: The system is a Majorana tetron (four Majorana zero modes) coupled to an auxiliary quantum dot. The dynamics are analyzed using effective two-level Hamiltonians derived from the full coupled dot-tetron system.
key_observables: Interwire X-parity lifetime and X-parity switching time.
important_parameters: Noise strengths (e.g., $1/f$ noise), bare-tetron coherence time ($T_2^*$), and the coupling strength to the measurement dot.
main_assumptions: The analysis considers noise sources from both the readout dot potential and the residual Majorana splittings, and it analyzes the system in two distinct coupling regimes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides a schematic of the dot-tetron model in the X-measurement configuration, illustrating the nanowires, MZMs, the dot, and the coupling terms.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the coupled dot-tetron model and its dispersive description in an early section, followed by detailed calculations of the noise-induced X-parity dynamics in subsequent sections.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses decoherence mitigation in topological qubits by showing that the act of measurement itself can enhance coherence, a crucial concept for scalable quantum computation.
